LAB isolated from dairy products exhibited lipolytic, lipolytic and antibacteric activities and that the enzymes were mainly located in the cell wall and extracellular space.
the lipases, protease, and antibacterial protein from LAB are important for the functionality of food and human health.
LAB strains isolated from dairy products were screened for their lipolytic, and proteolytic and anti-microbial activities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of LAB strains that may offer improved functionality to dairy products and to the human gut microbiome.
understanding how LAB strains with high enzyme activities contribute to the health-promoting benefits of fermented dairy products.
the identification of LAB strains with enhanced enzymatic activity for the development of novel probiotic dairy products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LAB strains isolated in this study have the potential for use as probiotics, as well as in the production of fermented dairy products.
the LAB strains isolated from various dairy products are capable of exhibiting high enzymatic activities and may be used as starter cultures in fermentative processes.

LAB isolated from various types of dairy products can be a good source of lipases, protease, and antibacterial protein, which may be further used to improve the quality of dairy products and human health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LAB strains isolated from dairy products may be potential producers of lipases, protease and antibacterial proteins and may offer improved functionality in foods and human gut microbiota.
LAB from diverse dairy sources are potential producers of lipases, proteolytic enzymes and antibacterial proteins that may be useful for food applications and human health.
we isolated and identified LAB with enhanced enzymatic activity and characterized the subcellular distribution of their lipases and proteases, and the antibacterial proteins they produced.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LAB isolated from dairy products are promising candidates for the production of lipolytic and antibacterially active enzymes.
the enzymatic properties of LAB can be enhanced by screening and selection of strains from different dairy products, which can improve their potential applications in foods and human health.
the LAB strains with enhanced enzymatic properties can be used in fermented food products to improve their digestibility and nutritional quality.
